exposure: postnatal age at TEOAE screening (less than 24, 24-36, 36-48, >48 hours)
cohort: The study included 408 neonates at low risk of hearing impairment.
finding: Screening for newborn hearing at greater than or equal to 48 hours postnatal age significantly improved TEOAE pass rates.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with a delayed passing time for newborn hearing screening compared with vaginal delivery.
followup_time: More than 48 hours (for screening pass rates); 1 month (for persistent failures)
